assessment.nobel_worthiness: Strong claim on formal and linguistic achievement. His poetry and essays remake modern Arabic verse through myth, fragmentation and a sustained dialogue with the classical tradition. Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses show a distinctive voice and intellectual depth. His critical work on tradition and modernity adds significance beyond individual collections.
assessment.attribution: The credited name is the single writer Adonis. A citation could cover the renewal of Arabic poetic language and the poetry-and-criticism project as one body of work. The scope is clear and needs no additional names.
assessment.maturity: A very long, sustained career with a well-established body of work and wide influence on later Arabic poetry. Timing is not an issue for the oeuvre, which is fully formed.
uncertainties: Poetry in translation loses much of the prosodic and intertextual work that is central to his claim, so my assessment relies on secondary accounts of the Arabic.
Coverage of his essays and critical prose is uneven in translation.
Political and public-intellectual positions should not stand in for literary merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visionary, densely patterned prose with a very distinctive voice. Memory, the body and metaphysical speculation are built into large architectures such as Blinding and Solenoid. The imaginative ambition and formal control are high, and his work fits a tradition of expansive European modernism and the fantastic.
assessment.attribution: A single named writer. The citation scope would plausibly be the visionary, encyclopedic prose project across fiction, with poetry as a secondary strand. It is clear and unconflicted.
assessment.maturity: Decades of sustained work, with the major novels showing increasing scale. The oeuvre appears consolidated, and the late works extend rather than repeat the earlier ones.
uncertainties: Translation quality and coverage of the very long novels, and of his poetry, are uncertain and affect how well the prose density carries over.
I cannot independently verify how consistently the quality holds across the full corpus.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A major poetic project. Large sequences such as Purgatory and Anteparadise, along with landscape-scale interventions, convert historical suffering and dictatorship-era trauma into collective memorial form. The formal ambition and the fusion of the personal, the visionary and the political are distinctive.
assessment.attribution: A single poet. The citation would concern poetry of memory and collective witness, with the land and visual interventions as part of the poetic practice. The scope is coherent.
assessment.maturity: A long career of sustained engagement with the same large themes, with accumulated cohesion. Timing is unproblematic.
uncertainties: Poetry in translation, especially the visual and typographic dimensions, is difficult to judge.
The land and sky interventions are works whose literary status needs careful weighing.
Historical-political significance must not substitute for literary assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: An uncompromising, original voice. Dreamlike narrative worlds destabilize psychology, space and causality, which makes her one of the most formally radical contemporary Chinese-language writers. Imaginative depth is high, though the work is demanding and heterogeneous in effect.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. The citation could cover radical experimental fiction in Chinese, including the novels and short fiction. The scope is clear.
assessment.maturity: Several decades of consistent output with a recognizable and evolving method. The oeuvre appears substantial, though quality across the entire corpus is hard to gauge.
uncertainties: Translation is a particular risk, since the work depends on estrangement effects in Chinese, and only part of the corpus is available in English.
Critical reception is divided on whether the method sustains itself across so many works.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large polyphonic narratives such as Carpentaria and The Swan Book remake the novel through Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time. Voice, scale and imaginative reach are distinctive, and her nonfiction on Aboriginal history adds intellectual substance.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. The citation could address renewal of the novel through Indigenous storytelling and political imagination. It is clear, though the fiction rests on a few major books.
assessment.maturity: A strong body of work, but with fewer major novels than several other candidates. The depth is notable, and the question is whether the oeuvre has reached its full breadth.
uncertainties: The number of major works is smaller than for many candidates, which affects the sustained-quality assessment.
Her work is written in English, but the Indigenous oral and linguistic contexts it draws on are only partly accessible to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Encyclopedic fiction linking systems of power, scientific knowledge and countercultural imagination. Gravity's Rainbow and Mason & Dixon are landmark works of postwar fiction, with great linguistic range and formal ambition.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. The citation could address the encyclopedic novel of systems and paranoia. The scope is clear, though the later works are uneven in reception.
assessment.maturity: A long career with an established canon and wide influence. The central achievement is secure, though the quality of the latest novels is more contested.
uncertainties: Critical opinion on the later novels is mixed, and I cannot independently verify it.
The density and cultural specificity may complicate translation and committee consensus.
Fame and reputation must not stand in for assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hybrid travel, essay and fiction map Europe through borderlands, memory and intellectual history. Danube and Microcosms combine erudition with a humane narrative voice. The achievement is real and distinctive in form, though more scholarly and essayistic than the strongest candidates.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. The citation could be framed around the Central European literary-essayistic project. The scope is coherent.
assessment.maturity: A long career with consolidated work. Some of the work depends on a particular Central European cultural horizon, which affects how far it travels.
uncertainties: The essayistic and scholarly components are harder to place within a purely literary comparison.
Translation of the erudite, allusive prose carries risk.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A desert cosmology joining Tuareg experience, ecological limits and metaphysical fiction. Gold Dust and The Bleeding of the Stone show a distinctive imaginative world and mythic register, with real depth of vision in a very large body of Arabic fiction.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. The citation could address mythic and ecological fiction rooted in Tuareg culture and written in Arabic. The scope is clear.
assessment.maturity: A very large, long-running oeuvre with a consistent world. Repetitiveness across so many books is a question for sustained quality.
uncertainties: Translation coverage of this large corpus is incomplete and varies in quality, so my judgement of the whole is limited.
I cannot verify how varied the work is across the large number of books.
